label: 9–15 November
notes: Cook in number order: sea bass and prawns first while they're freshest.
Breakfast is for one this week: the same pancakes every morning, about 12 minutes.
This week uses up the chicken and mince in the freezer. From now on, proteins are bought only for that week.
Menu approved by you on Friday with the toggles. 3 swapped to the glazed chicken & aubergine.
Nutrition is estimated per serving from ingredient weights.

breakfast.title: GF oat protein pancakes with berries & chia (for 1)

steps.text: Mix 30g oats, 1 egg, 60g yoghurt and ⅛ tsp salt in a bowl. Leave 5 min so the oats soften.
Microwave the berries in a mug for 1 min until warm and juicy.
Heat ½ tsp oil in a non-stick pan on medium. Spoon in 3 small pancakes and cook 2 min per side, until golden and set in the middle.
Top with 40g yoghurt, the berries and 1 tsp chia.

breakfast.tip: Breakfast is for one: 5 mornings use 5 eggs, 150g oats, 500g yoghurt and 400g berries.

dinners.title: Lemon-garlic sea bass with herby lentils, roast tomatoes & spinach

ingredients.item: olive oil (1 tsp tomatoes, 1 tsp fish, 1 tbsp lentils)
salt (¼ lentils, ⅛ tomatoes, ¼ fish, ⅛ dressing)

steps.text: Lentils: rinse 60g lentils. Put them in a pan with 400ml water and ¼ tsp salt. Bring to the boil, then simmer uncovered for 20–25 min, until soft but still holding their shape. Drain.
Air Fryer: toss the halved tomatoes with 1 tsp oil and ⅛ tsp salt. Cook at 200°C for 10 min, until soft and blistered. Tip them into a bowl.
Fish: pat the fillets dry. Rub the flesh side with 1 tsp oil, the zest of the lemon, 1 grated garlic clove, ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper.
Air Fryer: fish skin-side down at 200°C for 6–7 min. Done when the flesh is opaque all through and flakes with a fork.

Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp oil in the lentil pan on medium. Add the sliced garlic for 1 min until pale gold, then the drained lentils, the spinach and the other grated garlic clove. Stir 2 min until the spinach wilts.
Off the heat, stir in 30ml lemon juice, most of the parsley, ⅛ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper.
Taste the lentils: if flat, add ⅛ tsp salt and 1 tsp lemon juice. Serve: lentils, tomatoes, 2 fillets each, last of the parsley.

dinners.tip: Sea bass fillets are thin: check at 6 min. Lentils soak up salt and lemon, so taste them after dressing.

dinners.title: Greek garlic prawns with tomato & feta (saganaki), rice

steps.text: Rice: rinse 100g rice for 30 sec. Pan with 175ml water and ¼ tsp salt. Bring to the boil, lid on, lowest heat 10 min, then off the heat with the lid on for 5 min.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a frying pan on medium for 1 min. Add the onion and cook 5 min until soft. Add the garlic, 1 tsp oregano and ¼ tsp chilli flakes for 1 min.
Add the tomatoes, ¼ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Simmer 10 min, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
Pat the prawns dry and stir them in. Simmer 3–4 min, until pink all through and curled into a C.
Off the heat: scatter over the feta and most of the parsley, and squeeze over 15ml lemon juice.
Taste the sauce: feta adds salt, so only add ⅛ tsp more if it's flat. Too sharp? ½ tsp honey. Serve over the rice with the last parsley.

dinners.tip: Keep the sauce at a gentle bubble once the prawns are in: hard boiling makes them rubbery.

dinners.title: Tamari-honey glazed chicken & aubergine with rice and garlicky green beans

ingredients.item: chicken thigh fillets (from the freezer, defrosted in the fridge)
garlic (2 for the glaze, 1 for the beans)
olive oil (2 tsp aubergine, 1 tsp chicken, 1 tsp beans)
salt (¼ rice, ⅛ beans): the tamari seasons the chicken and aubergine

steps.text: Rice: rinse 100g rice. Pan with 175ml water and ¼ tsp salt, boil, lid on, lowest heat 10 min, then 5 min off the heat.
Air Fryer: toss the aubergine cubes with 2 tsp oil. Cook at 200°C for 12 min, shaking at 6, until soft and browned. Tip into a bowl.
Rub the chicken with 1 tsp oil and air fry at 200°C for 14 min, turning at 7 min.
Glaze: in a small pan, simmer 45ml tamari, 1 tbsp honey, 30ml water, the ginger and 2 grated garlic cloves for 2–3 min, until syrupy and coating a spoon.

Brush half the glaze over the chicken, add the aubergine back next to it and air fry 2 min more. Chicken is done at 75°C in the thickest part, or when the juices run clear. Toss the aubergine in the rest of the glaze.

Beans: heat 1 tsp oil in a frying pan on high. Add the beans with 2 tbsp water and ⅛ tsp salt and cook 4 min, until bright green and just tender. Add the last grated garlic clove for the final 30 sec.
Slice the chicken 1cm thick. Serve: rice, aubergine, chicken, beans, spring onions on top.
Taste: if flat, add 1 tsp tamari over the rice. Too salty? A squeeze of lemon.

dinners.tip: The day before, move the chicken from the freezer to the fridge. No salt on the chicken or aubergine: 3 tbsp tamari carries about 1 tsp salt.

dinners.title: Spiced beef stuffed peppers with rice & garlic yoghurt

ingredients.item: lean beef mince 5%, defrosted in the fridge
olive oil (1 tsp mince, 1 tsp peppers)
salt (¼ rice, ½ filling, ⅛ yoghurt)

steps.text: Rice: rinse 60g rice. Pan with 120ml water and ¼ tsp salt, boil, lid on, lowest heat 10 min, then 5 min off the heat.
Air Fryer: rub the pepper halves with 1 tsp oil and cook cut-side down at 190°C for 8 min, to soften.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a frying pan on high. Brown the mince for 5 min, breaking it up, until no pink is left. Turn to medium, add the onion for 4 min.

Add the garlic, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp oregano, ¼ tsp chilli flakes and 1 tbsp tomato paste for 1 min. Add ½ tin tomatoes, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper and simmer 5 min until thick. Stir in the rice.
Taste the filling now: if flat, ⅛ tsp salt; if sharp, ½ tsp honey.
Turn the peppers cut-side up, pack in the filling and air fry at 190°C for 8 min, until the tops are browned and the peppers are soft at the edges.
Yoghurt: stir 60g yoghurt with ½ grated garlic clove, 1 tsp lemon juice and ⅛ tsp salt. Serve 3 halves each with a spoon of yoghurt and the parsley.

dinners.tip: This uses all the mince in the freezer, so protein comes in above the usual 30–40g. The day before, move both bags to the fridge. Freeze the other ½ tin of tomatoes in a box, or use it within 3 days.

dinners.title: Potato, spinach & feta frittata with tomato & red onion salad

ingredients.item: red onion (½ sliced for the frittata, ½ very thin for the salad)
salt (1 tsp potato water, ¼ eggs, ⅛ salad)

steps.text: Boil 1 litre water with 1 tsp salt. Add the potato slices and boil 8 min, until a knife slides in. Drain.
Heat 2 tsp oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan (with a lid) on medium. Cook the sliced ½ onion 4 min, add the potatoes for 3 min, then the spinach for 1 min until wilted. Spread everything out evenly.
Beat the 7 eggs with ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper. Pour over, scatter the feta on top. Lid on, low heat, 10–12 min, until the edges are set and the middle only just wobbles.
Salad: mix the tomatoes with the thin ½ onion, 1 tsp oil, 1 tsp lemon juice, ⅛ tsp salt, ⅛ tsp pepper and the parsley.
Rest the frittata 2 min, slide it out and cut in half. Taste a bite: if flat, a little more salad dressing; feta adds salt, so no more on the eggs.

dinners.tip: Low heat and a lid cook the top without flipping. If the middle is still runny after 12 min, give it 2 more.

tips: Sea bass and prawns go in the coldest part of the fridge: they're 1 and 2.
Wrap the parsley in damp kitchen roll in a box.
The emergency cupboard extras (tins, frozen spinach, hash browns) are stock, not part of this week's recipes. Put them at the back.
Optional: cook 3's rice at the same time. 200g rice, 350ml water, ½ tsp salt. Fridge 3's half within 1 hour; reheat once only, until piping hot.
Move the 300g chicken thighs from the freezer to the fridge.
Move both bags of beef mince (390g) from the freezer to the fridge. This clears the freezer of meat.
Baby potatoes: 250g used in 5, about 750g left for the weekend (or roast with the hash browns).
Feta: 120g used, 80g left: crumble over breakfast or salads.
Chopped tomatoes: 1½ tins used from the 6; 4 are the emergency stock. Freeze the spare ½ tin from 4.
Lemons: 1 in 1, ½ in 2, a little in 4 and 5: about 1½ left.
